tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## claude.ai Context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, porting code between libraries, platforms, or SQL dialects, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, debugging, or reviewing code that does not depend on a library or platform API, or general programming concepts.

## claude.ai Sentry
Use Sentry tools for questions about the user's production apps or Sentry account: errors, crashes, issues, stack traces, traces, spans, slow requests, logs, metrics, replays, profiles, releases, monitors, alert rules, and Sentry SDK setup and docs.
- For a Sentry URL or an issue, event, trace, or replay ID, call get_sentry_resource first.
- Do not look up the organization first; tools default to it when the user has one. Read `org/project` notation as the organization and project slugs. If a tool asks for organizationSlug, call find_organizations and pass the slug and regionUrl it returns.
- search_issues finds grouped problems ("what's broken", "top issues"); search_errors, search_logs, search_traces, search_metrics, search_profiles, search_replays find individual events, counts, and aggregates.

## claude.ai Slack
Before posting a new message to a Slack channel the user didn't name, read its topic and description with slack_search_channels, and if they say that kind of message belongs elsewhere, tell the user instead of posting.

## claude.ai Typefully - Social Media Scheduler
Create, schedule, and publish social media posts with Typefully across X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, and Substack, and read post analytics.

## easel
Tools registered by the cc-plugin-easel plugin through $.tool.register.

## plugin:polygraph:polygraph-mcp
Polygraph MCP server — provides tools for coordinating cross-repository changes via Polygraph.

Use whoami to inspect auth state and login to authenticate with a token if needed. Use list_repos when you need to discover or choose repositories, start_session to start a session, add_repo to add explicitly named repositories directly, and the remaining tools to manage the session lifecycle.

A repository can run multiple child agents at once, distinguished by an optional role: pass role to spawn_agent, show_agent, stop_agent, allow_agent, or deny_agent to target a specific agent. Omitting role targets the default role — exactly the pre-role single-agent behavior, and the only role whose logs are uploaded/multiplexed to the cloud; view a non-default agent locally with `polygraph agent attach <repo> --role <role>`.

Resuming an AI agent session is reconnecting to restore context only. After you resume, do not make any changes until the user explicitly asks for changes.

# SpeedDev cloud session

These files come from the SpeedDev cockpit plugin. `<cockpit skill folder>` in them is the base directory the cockpit skill was loaded from.

cockpit: 23

The routine started you with a payload: the `<routine-fire-payload>` block
below the saved prompt. Its lines say what to do; this file says how to read
them. Report to SpeedDev through the cockpit skill (`SKILL.md` next to this
file) and nothing else.

## Cockpit version

The `cockpit:` line at the top of this file is the version of the cockpit
files in this repo; the payload's `cockpit:` line is the routine's. When the
payload's number is higher, these files are older than the routine, and
every payload except for a "SpeedDev test" one does this:

1. First post one milestone (skill, "Decisions and milestones",
   `"art":"meilenstein"`) on the payload's `work item:`, with `<own>` and
   `<payload>` filled in:
   "Cockpit plugin outdated (plugin <own>, routine <payload>): sync the speeddev marketplace under claude.ai Customize > Plugins, or download the cockpit plugin again from the setup page and upload it to claude.ai."

6dcf08fb chore(release): 74.172.5 ## Problem `feat-shared-bacteria-engine` (`libs/features/bacteria-engine`, 25.7k LOC source, 14.1k spec at `3da81ae`) started as "the game's engine without Angular" (#2482) and has since become the place for everything the game, its Cloud Functions and the admin share. Three unrelated concerns now sit in it: 1. **The simulation and its replays**: `bacteria-simulation.ts` (1569), `match-engine.ts` (923), `replay.ts` (1024), `match-run.ts`, `grid/`, `gpu-int/`, the bots, the maps and level generator. 2. **The cloud contract** between the game, the functions and the admin: `boards.ts`, `attempts.ts`, `admin-commands.ts`, `command-documents.ts`, `cloud-records/`, `xp.ts`, `ranks.ts`, `feature-toggles.ts`, `daily.ts`, `social/`. 3. **The UI's texts**: `src/lib/i18n/en/*.ts` and `i18n/de/*.ts`, 3,183 lines in 21 files a language (`menu.ts`, `help.ts`, `settings.ts`, `support.ts`, `controls.ts`, …), almost all of them texts only the Angular game shows. Evidence that they are lumped together rather than layered: - `src/lib/state/` is **one flat folder of 76 source files (16,025 LOC)** beside five sub-folders; `replay-score.ts`, `skins.ts`, `base64.ts`, `admin-commands.ts` and `bacteria-simulation.ts` are siblings. 42 of the 76 files import nothing of the simulation, the match or a replay. - `src/index.ts` is **791 lines with 158 `export … from` statements**: one public surface for all three concerns, so no consumer says which part it depends on. - The functions use the texts not at all: of everything under `i18n/` and `site/`, `apps/bacteria-wars-functions` imports only `LOCALES` and `inLang`. Of the simulation it needs `replayVerdict`, `replayFromBytes` and a few constants; most of its 110-odd imported symbols are the cloud contract (`parseBoardId`, `dailySort`, `parseBan`, `CommandResult`, `xpOf`, …). Because Nx sees one project, a change to any of the three counts as a change to all: - The `perf` target's inputs are `production`, `^production` and `tools/perf/**`. Rewording a German menu text in `i18n/de/menu.ts` reruns the engine benchmark (about 1.5 minutes, alone on its worker, `parallelism: false`), the golden replay specs and `engine-bundle.spec.ts`. - `bacteria-wars-functions:deploy` reads the engine through `^production`, so, as CLAUDE.md already notes, "every change to the game's engine" redeploys the functions with `--force`, a text change included, although no function renders one of those texts. ## Why it matters for modularity A `feat-shared` lib with fan-in 4 (game, functions, admin through the game, tools) should be the stable core. Here its most volatile content (texts) and its most sensitive content (the deterministic simulation, guarded by goldens, `BALANCE_VERSION` and a performance gate) share a boundary, so the gates meant for the simulation fire for copy edits and a production deploy of server code follows from UI wording. The single barrel also hides which of the 158 exports are a contract with the server and which are internals of the match. ## Proposed change In steps, each its own PR: 1. **Texts out of the engine.** Move `i18n/en/`, `i18n/de/` and `dictionaries.ts` to a lib of their own (`libs/features/bacteria-texts`, `feat-shared-bacteria-texts`, tag `feat-shared`), which the game lib depends on. The engine keeps the mechanics (`translation.ts`, `language.ts`, `game-text.ts`). `GameText.key` is typed `TranslationKey = EntryPath` today (`game-text.ts:1`), which is the one coupling to cut: the engine types the keys it emits itself (a union of its own keys, or a generic parameter), and a spec in the texts lib fails when a key the engine emits has no text in either language. 2. **Folders by concern in `state/`**: `simulation/` (simulation, match engine, bots, weapons, zones), `replay/`, `levels/` (maps, generator, campaign, training), `progress/` (evolution, unlocks, achievements, medallions, xp) and `cloud/` (boards, attempts, commands, cloud records, toggles). No API change. 3. **An entry point for the cloud contract**, as `/balance` and `/testing` already are: `@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine/cloud`, taken by the functions and the admin kit for everything that is a document shape, an id or a sort. `src/index.ts` shrinks accordingly. 4. Optional, once 2 is done: narrow `perf`'s inputs from `production` to the folders the bench plays. ```mermaid flowchart LR game["feat-lazy-bacteria-game"] --> texts["feat-shared-bacteria-texts
en/, de/"] game --> engine["feat-shared-bacteria-engine
simulation · replay · levels · progress"] game --> cloud["…/cloud entry
boards, commands, cloud records"] functions["bacteria-wars-functions"] --> cloud functions --> engine texts -. "keys checked by spec" .-> engine ``` ## Effort Step 1: M. Step 2: M (mechanical moves, many import paths). Step 3: M. ## Risk - Step 1 changes how translation keys are typed; a key that loses its compile-time check must get the spec's check instead. The public replay pages (`apps/bacteria-wars-functions/src/site/`) keep their own texts and are not affected. - A new lib has to be skipped in `tools/federation/workspace-federation.js` in all four apps together with the engine. - Steps 2 and 3 must not change what the simulation computes: the golden replays (`golden-replay.spec.ts`), the GPU goldens and the `perf` checksums are the proof, with no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A change only to a text under the texts lib makes neither `feat-shared-bacteria-engine:perf` nor `bacteria-wars-functions:deploy` affected (`tools/ci/release-affected.mjs` on such a diff selects no functions deploy). - [ ] `libs/features/bacteria-engine/src/lib/state/` holds no more than a handful of files at its top level; each concern has a folder. - [ ] The functions import document shapes, ids and sorts from the `/cloud` entry; `src/index.ts` is well under half its 791 lines. - [ ] Golden replays, GPU goldens and the `perf` checksums are unchanged. - [ ] `docs/architecture/README.md` shows no cycle and no tag violation. See [Modularity metrics](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/blob/main/docs/architecture/README.md#modularity-metrics) (`feat-shared-bacteria-engine`: fan-in 4, instability 0.2) and the [project dependency graph](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/blob/main/docs/architecture/README.md#project-dependency-graph). Related: #3102 (the rendering out of the game lib). Tracked in #2370 docs/plans/3103-arch-feat-shared-bacteria-engine-mixes-simulation-cloud-contract-and-3-2k-lines-of-ui-texts-behind-one-791-line-barrel.md docs/specs/3103-arch-feat-shared-bacteria-engine-mixes-simulation-cloud-contract-and-3-2k-lines-of-ui-texts-behind-one-791-line-barrel.md 90 docs/specs/3103-arch-feat-shared-bacteria-engine-mixes-simulation-cloud-contract-and-3-2k-lines-of-ui-texts-behind-one-791-line-barrel.md 20 docs/plans/3103-arch-feat-shared-bacteria-engine-mixes-simulation-cloud-contract-and-3-2k-lines-of-ui-texts-behind-one-791-line-barrel.md 110 total

{"ok":true}{"ok":true}# Bacteria engine: the UI texts out of the engine

Issue: [#3103](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/3103)

## Goal

`feat-shared-bacteria-engine` holds the game's UI texts (`src/lib/i18n/en/`, `de/`, 3,183 lines in 21 areas a language) next to the deterministic simulation. Every copy edit therefore reruns the engine's `perf` gate, its golden specs and `engine-bundle.spec.ts`, and redeploys `bacteria-wars-functions` (`--force`), although no function shows these texts.

This change is step 1 of the issue: the texts the engine does not render leave the engine, so a change to one of them affects neither `feat-shared-bacteria-engine` nor `bacteria-wars-functions`.

## Non-goals

- Steps 2 to 4 of the issue (folders by concern in `state/`, the `/cloud` entry, narrower `perf` inputs). They follow as later PRs of [#3103](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/3103) (see Decided questions).
- No change to a text, a key path or what a screen shows.
- No change to what the simulation computes: no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump, goldens unchanged.
- The public replay pages' texts (`apps/bacteria-wars-functions/src/site/`) and the admin's own dictionaries stay as they are.

## What the code shows

- The engine **renders English at runtime**: `english()` (`i18n/game-text.ts`) fills `Achievement.name`/`condition`, `GameMap.name` of a generated level, `XpPart.label`, `ONLINE_LOCKS`, `ladderLocks`, the medallion and win-condition hints and the unlock locks, from the dictionary `EN`. The keys it builds come from four areas only: `achievements`, `game`, `levels` and `training` (457 of the 1,593 English lines).
- The game builds `GameText`s of its own with keys of other areas (`boards`, `online`, `settings`, `newGame`, …), so `GameText.key` cannot simply narrow to the engine's keys.
- Module boundaries (`.oxlintrc.json`): `feat-shared` may depend only on `shared`, `utils`, `api`; the game (`feature:lazy`) only on `feat-shared`, `shared`, `utils`, `api`. A new `feat-shared` texts lib could therefore not import the engine's English areas or its `Translation` type, and a `feature` texts lib could not be imported by the game.

## Decisions

1. **The engine keeps the English texts it renders, nothing else.** `en/achievements.ts`, `en/game.ts`, `en/levels.ts`, `en/training.ts` stay in the engine as `ENGINE_EN` (`i18n/engine-texts.ts`) with `EngineTextKey = EntryPath<typeof ENGINE_EN>`; `english()` renders from it. Reason: the engine stores these strings in its state (a generated level's map name, an achievement's name), so they are engine output; moving them out would mean changing every consumer of those fields first (about 110 lines in the game), a larger change better made on its own if wanted.
2. **All other texts move into the game lib**, `libs/features/lazy/bacteria-game/src/lib/i18n/texts/`: the 17 other English areas, all 21 German areas (the German ones of the engine's four areas typed `Translation<typeof …>` against the engine's English, so a missing or extra German key still fails to compile), and `dictionaries.ts` with `EN` (the engine's four areas plus the game's), `DE`, `DICTIONARIES` and `TranslationKey`. Reason: the game is their only consumer (the admin takes `TranslationKey` through the game's `admin-kit`), it already depends on the engine, and it needs no new tag rule. The issue's own lib (`feat-shared-bacteria-texts`) would need either `feat-shared → feat-shared` or a new tag allowed for `feature:lazy`, plus a federation skip in all four apps, for no consumer beyond the game.
3. **`GameText` becomes generic over its key**: `GameText<K extends string = EngineTextKey>`, `Translate<K>` and `renderGameText<K>` likewise; `english()` takes the engine's `GameText` only. The game defines its `GameText` as `GameText<TranslationKey>` from `i18n/game-texts.ts`, its existing text module, and its files import it from there. An engine `GameText` is assignable to the game's, since `EngineTextKey` is a subset of `TranslationKey`, so the key check stays at compile time on both sides.
4. **The engine's index** stops exporting `DE`, `DICTIONARIES`, `EN` and `TranslationKey` and exports `ENGINE_EN` instead (plus the generic `GameText`; `GameTextParams`, `Translate` and `EngineTextKey` stay internal, as nothing outside uses them). The mechanics (`translation.ts`, `language.ts`, `game-text.ts`) stay.
5. **Docs**: the engine's and the game's `CLAUDE.md` say where texts live and that a text the engine renders goes into its four areas. `docs/architecture/README.md` stays as it is: the change adds no project and no dependency (the game already depends on the engine), and the diagrams' drift since their last run is refreshed by its own PR ([#3101](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/3101)).

## Acceptance

1. A diff changing only a file under `libs/features/lazy/bacteria-game/src/lib/i18n/texts/` makes neither `feat-shared-bacteria-engine` nor `bacteria-wars-functions` affected (`nx show projects --affected` on that diff), and `tools/ci/release-affected.mjs` on it selects no functions deploy.
2. The engine holds no German text and no English area it does not render: `libs/features/bacteria-engine/src/lib/i18n/` has no `de/` and only the four English areas.
3. A German area missing a key, or holding one too many, still fails to compile (spec-typecheck or build of the game).
4. Every key and every text is unchanged: a JSON dump of `EN` and `DE` taken before the move equals the one after it (checked during the work, noted in the PR, not committed).
5. Golden replays (`golden-replay.spec.ts`), GPU goldens and the `perf` checksums are unchanged; no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump.
6. `npx nx affected -t lint,lint-templates,test,typecheck-specs,build` green; no new project or dependency edge, so no cycle and no tag violation (boundaries lint green).

## Decided questions

- **Scope** (manager, request 1239): this PR delivers step 1 and leaves [#3103](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/3103) open (`Part of [#3103](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/3103)`). Steps 2 to 4 stay later PRs of [#3103](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/3103), no sub-issues.
- **Texts in the game lib** instead of a lib of their own (decision 2): approved as written.

# Step 2: folders by concern in `state/`

Step 1 landed in [#3118](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/pull/3118). This section is the spec for step 2.

## Goal (step 2)

`libs/features/bacteria-engine/src/lib/state/` is one flat folder of 76 source files (with their specs and three data files) beside five sub-folders. After this step each concern has a folder of its own and the top level keeps only the three helpers every concern uses, so a reader sees which part of the engine a file belongs to before opening it, and step 3 can name the cloud contract's files by folder.

## Non-goals (step 2)

- No API change: `src/index.ts`, `src/balance.ts` and `src/testing.ts` export exactly the same names; only their `from` paths change. No consumer outside the engine changes an import (none imports a path inside it).
- No code change inside a moved file beyond its import paths: no rename of a file or symbol, no split, no merge.
- No change to what the simulation computes: goldens, GPU goldens and the `perf` checksums unchanged, no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump.
- Steps 3 (the `/cloud` entry) and 4 (narrower `perf` inputs) stay later PRs.
- The old specs and plans under `docs/` keep the paths they were written with (they record what was true then).

## Decisions (step 2)

1. **Six folders, not the issue's five.** The issue puts the match engine and the bots into `simulation/`; that folder would hold 31 files, the flat folder again. `simulation/` is the deterministic physics both rulesets share (what `gpu-int` mirrors and the goldens pin); `match/` is the loop around it: the engine, its run, setup, win conditions, the bots and the computer opponent.
2. **The map** (every spec, JSON and folder moves with its file):

   | Folder        | Files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
   | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | `simulation/` | `bacteria-simulation`, `simulation`, `simulation-provider`, `simulation-report`, `grid-format`, `cells`, `arena-fixtures`, `arena-size`, `nutrient-pellets`, `weapon-effects`, `evolution`, `game-balance`, `fixed-tick`; the folders `gpu-int/` and `grid/`                                                                                        |
   | `match/`      | `match-engine`, `match-run`, `match-setup`, `game-mode`, `frame-pacer`, `win-conditions`, `checksum`, `perf-probe`, `bot-controller`, `bot-navigation`, `bot-senses`, `recent-cache`, `neutral-brain` (with `neutral-colonies.spec`), `computer-opponent`, `expected-player`, `difficulty-curve`, `rivalry`, `player.model`, `evolution-match.spec` |
   | `levels/`     | `maps`, `expanse-maps`, `organic-maps`, `outbreak-maps`, `reactor-maps`, `shapes`, `zones`, `game-maps`, `training-levels`, `levels`, `match-level`, `campaign`, `chapters`, `daily`, `endless`, `training`; `level-generator/` as `levels/generator/`                                                                                              |
   | `replay/`     | `replay`, `replay-id`, `replay-link`, `replay-pack`, `replay-reasons`, `replay-score`, `replay-verdict`, `ghost`, `golden-replay.json` with `golden-replay.spec`, `golden-match.spec`                                                                                                                                                               |
   | `progress/`   | `achievement-ids`, `achievements`, `medallions`, `xp`, `earnings`, `progress`, `evolution-progress`, `unlocks`, `ranks`, `skins`, `colony-colors`, `colony-looks`, `play-games-achievements.json` with its spec                                                                                                                                     |
   | `cloud/`      | `boards`, `attempts`, `ranked-match`, `admin-commands`, `command-documents`, `feature-toggles`; `cloud-records/` as `cloud/records/`                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
   | top level     | `geometry`, `is-object`, `base64` (helpers of every concern); `balance/` stays (the `/balance` entry's lab)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

   Reasons for the borderline ones: `evolution` (the traits and weapons) and `fixed-tick` (the tick clock) are read by the physics itself; `difficulty-curve`, `expected-player` and `computer-opponent` choose the computer's strength, which is match setup; `colony-colors`, `colony-looks` and `skins` are unlocked looks; `match-level` picks an online match's level from the ladder; `ranked-match` is the declared attempt, next to `attempts`.

3. **The move is one mechanical commit, made by a script** (`git mv` per entry, then every relative specifier in `libs/features/bacteria-engine/src/**` recomputed from the old to the new location), so git shows renames and a reviewer can rerun it. The script lives in the scratchpad, not the repo: it is used once.
4. **Paths outside the engine** that name a moved file are updated in the same PR: `tools/perf/engine-bench.mjs` (the golden replay), `tools/bacteria-game/play-games.ts`, `apps/bacteria-wars-functions/src/replays/replays.emulator.ts` (the golden replay), `apps/bacteria-wars-android/README.md`, the root `CLAUDE.md`, the engine's and the game's `CLAUDE.md` and the game's `README.md` where they name an engine file.
5. **Release effect accepted**: the move touches the engine's sources, so its release redeploys `bacteria-wars-functions` and the game once, with code that behaves the same.

## Acceptance (step 2)

1. `state/` holds at its top level only `geometry.ts`, `is-object.ts` (with its spec), `base64.ts` and the folders `simulation/`, `match/`, `levels/`, `replay/`, `progress/`, `cloud/`, `balance/`.
2. `src/index.ts`, `src/balance.ts` and `src/testing.ts` export the same names as before (a sorted list of their exported names, compared before and after, noted in the PR).
3. `git diff -M --stat` shows every moved file as a rename; no moved file changes beyond its import lines.
4. Golden replays (`golden-replay.spec.ts`, `golden-match.spec.ts`), GPU goldens (`golden.spec.ts`, `sim-golden.spec.ts`, `self-test-golden.spec.ts`) and the `perf` checksums unchanged; no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump.
5. No path in the repo outside `docs/specs` and `docs/plans` names a moved file at its old place (`grep` over the old paths).
6. `npx nx affected -t lint,lint-templates,test,typecheck-specs,build` green, plus `npx nx run feat-shared-bacteria-engine:perf` and `bacteria-wars-functions:test`.
# Plan: the UI texts out of the bacteria engine

Spec: [docs/specs/3103-arch-feat-shared-bacteria-engine-mixes-simulation-cloud-contract-and-3-2k-lines-of-ui-texts-behind-one-791-line-barrel.md](../specs/3103-arch-feat-shared-bacteria-engine-mixes-simulation-cloud-contract-and-3-2k-lines-of-ui-texts-behind-one-791-line-barrel.md)

2. **Game: the texts move in.** `git mv` the 17 other English areas and all 21 German areas to `libs/features/lazy/bacteria-game/src/lib/i18n/texts/{en,de}/`, `dictionaries.ts` to `texts/dictionaries.ts` (importing the engine's four English areas through `ENGINE_EN`), the German areas' `Translation` types against the engine's English through the engine's index. The game's `game-texts.ts` exports `TranslationKey` and `GameText` (`GameText<TranslationKey>`); every game and admin-kit import of `EN`, `DE`, `DICTIONARIES`, `TranslationKey` and `GameText` takes them from there. Tests: the game's existing `game-texts.spec.ts`, `i18n.service.spec.ts`, `evolution.component.spec.ts` move with their imports; JSON dump compared.

3. **Docs**: engine and game `CLAUDE.md` (the root `CLAUDE.md` names no text location; `npm run arch:diagrams` shows only unrelated drift, refreshed by [#3101](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/3101)). Commit `docs(feat-shared-bacteria-engine): say where the game's texts live`.
4. **Checks**: `npx nx format:write`; `npx nx affected -t lint,lint-templates,test,typecheck-specs,build`; `nx run feat-shared-bacteria-engine:perf` checksums; a scratch diff touching one German text checked with `nx show projects --affected` and `node tools/ci/release-affected.mjs` (acceptance 1), then dropped.

# Step 2: folders by concern in `state/`

## Non-goals (step 2)

- No API change: `src/index.ts`, `src/balance.ts` and `src/testing.ts` export exactly the same names; only their `from` paths change. No consumer outside the engine changes an import (none imports a path inside it).
- No code change inside a moved file beyond its import paths: no rename of a file or symbol, no split, no merge.
- No change to what the simulation computes: goldens, GPU goldens and the `perf` checksums unchanged, no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump.
- Steps 3 (the `/cloud` entry) and 4 (narrower `perf` inputs) stay later PRs.
- The old specs and plans under `docs/` keep the paths they were written with (they record what was true then).

## Decisions (step 2)

1. **Six folders, not the issue's five.** The issue puts the match engine and the bots into `simulation/`; that folder would hold 31 files, the flat folder again. `simulation/` is the deterministic physics both rulesets share (what `gpu-int` mirrors and the goldens pin); `match/` is the loop around it: the engine, its run, setup, win conditions, the bots and the computer opponent.
2. **The map** (every spec, JSON and folder moves with its file):

   | Folder        | Files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
   | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | `simulation/` | `bacteria-simulation`, `simulation`, `simulation-provider`, `simulation-report`, `grid-format`, `cells`, `arena-fixtures`, `arena-size`, `nutrient-pellets`, `weapon-effects`, `evolution`, `game-balance`, `fixed-tick`; the folders `gpu-int/` and `grid/`                                                                                        |
   | `match/`      | `match-engine`, `match-run`, `match-setup`, `game-mode`, `frame-pacer`, `win-conditions`, `checksum`, `perf-probe`, `bot-controller`, `bot-navigation`, `bot-senses`, `recent-cache`, `neutral-brain` (with `neutral-colonies.spec`), `computer-opponent`, `expected-player`, `difficulty-curve`, `rivalry`, `player.model`, `evolution-match.spec` |
   | `levels/`     | `maps`, `expanse-maps`, `organic-maps`, `outbreak-maps`, `reactor-maps`, `shapes`, `zones`, `game-maps`, `training-levels`, `levels`, `match-level`, `campaign`, `chapters`, `daily`, `endless`, `training`; `level-generator/` as `levels/generator/`                                                                                              |
   | `replay/`     | `replay`, `replay-id`, `replay-link`, `replay-pack`, `replay-reasons`, `replay-score`, `replay-verdict`, `ghost`, `golden-replay.json` with `golden-replay.spec`, `golden-match.spec`                                                                                                                                                               |
   | `progress/`   | `achievement-ids`, `achievements`, `medallions`, `xp`, `earnings`, `progress`, `evolution-progress`, `unlocks`, `ranks`, `skins`, `colony-colors`, `colony-looks`, `play-games-achievements.json` with its spec                                                                                                                                     |
   | `cloud/`      | `boards`, `attempts`, `ranked-match`, `admin-commands`, `command-documents`, `feature-toggles`; `cloud-records/` as `cloud/records/`                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
   | top level     | `geometry`, `is-object`, `base64` (helpers of every concern); `balance/` stays (the `/balance` entry's lab)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

   Reasons for the borderline ones: `evolution` (the traits and weapons) and `fixed-tick` (the tick clock) are read by the physics itself; `difficulty-curve`, `expected-player` and `computer-opponent` choose the computer's strength, which is match setup; `colony-colors`, `colony-looks` and `skins` are unlocked looks; `match-level` picks an online match's level from the ladder; `ranked-match` is the declared attempt, next to `attempts`.

3. **The move is one mechanical commit, made by a script** (`git mv` per entry, then every relative specifier in `libs/features/bacteria-engine/src/**` recomputed from the old to the new location), so git shows renames and a reviewer can rerun it. The script lives in the scratchpad, not the repo: it is used once.
4. **Paths outside the engine** that name a moved file are updated in the same PR: `tools/perf/engine-bench.mjs` (the golden replay), `tools/bacteria-game/play-games.ts`, `apps/bacteria-wars-functions/src/replays/replays.emulator.ts` (the golden replay), `apps/bacteria-wars-android/README.md`, the root `CLAUDE.md`, the engine's and the game's `CLAUDE.md` and the game's `README.md` where they name an engine file.
5. **Release effect accepted**: the move touches the engine's sources, so its release redeploys `bacteria-wars-functions` and the game once, with code that behaves the same.

## Acceptance (step 2)

1. `state/` holds at its top level only `geometry.ts`, `is-object.ts` (with its spec), `base64.ts` and the folders `simulation/`, `match/`, `levels/`, `replay/`, `progress/`, `cloud/`, `balance/`.
2. `src/index.ts`, `src/balance.ts` and `src/testing.ts` export the same names as before (a sorted list of their exported names, compared before and after, noted in the PR).
3. `git diff -M --stat` shows every moved file as a rename; no moved file changes beyond its import lines.
4. Golden replays (`golden-replay.spec.ts`, `golden-match.spec.ts`), GPU goldens (`golden.spec.ts`, `sim-golden.spec.ts`, `self-test-golden.spec.ts`) and the `perf` checksums unchanged; no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump.
5. No path in the repo outside `docs/specs` and `docs/plans` names a moved file at its old place (`grep` over the old paths).
6. `npx nx affected -t lint,lint-templates,test,typecheck-specs,build` green, plus `npx nx run feat-shared-bacteria-engine:perf` and `bacteria-wars-functions:test`.

# Step 3: the `/cloud` entry

Step 2 landed in [#3129](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/pull/3129). This section is the spec for step 3.

## Goal (step 3)

The documents the game, `bacteria-wars-functions` and the admin exchange (the boards, the attempts, the commands, the cloud records and the feature toggles) are described in `state/cloud/`, but reach every consumer through the one main entry, so no import says whether it takes the contract with the server or the match's internals. After this step they come from `@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine/cloud`, and the main entry no longer exports them.

## What the code shows (step 3)

- The main index (`src/index.ts`, 815 lines) exports 658 names: 126 from `state/cloud/` (154 lines), 84 of the GPU mirror (`simulation/gpu-int/`, `simulation/grid/`, `grid-format`, about 120 lines, used only by `feat-bacteria-rendering` and the game's GPU path), 448 others.
- Outside the engine, the cloud names are imported by `bacteria-wars-functions` (about 25 files), the game lib (about 32 files, `admin-kit.ts` included, which hands them on to the admin) and `bacteria-game-remote`'s `firestore-rules-toggles.spec.ts`. 21 of the 126 are imported by nobody outside the engine (`canDeclare`, `requiredAttempt`, `ToMillis`, `REPLAY_COMMAND_TYPES`, `XP_RISE_BASE`, …).
- `state/cloud/` imports from `simulation/`, `levels/`, `progress/`, `replay/` and `social/profile` (an attempt's level and arena, a board's tick cap, the avatar count). An entry of the same project may: the boundary rule counts the entry as the engine.
- The other entries (`/balance`, `/testing`) are a `src/<name>.ts` with a path in `tsconfig.base.json`; the engine's `build` (ng-packagr) builds `src/index.ts` only, and `tsconfig.lib.json` includes every non-spec `.ts`, so its `typecheck` covers a new entry file too. `engine-bundle.spec.ts` bundles `index.ts` alone.

## Decisions (step 3)

1. **The entry is the folder.** `src/cloud.ts` exports what `state/cloud/` (with `records/`) holds and something outside the engine imports, nothing else; the main index drops every name of that folder. `social/profile` (the player's profile document) stays in the main entry: the game's UI uses it for names and avatars as much as the server for its document, and it lives outside `state/cloud/`. Reason: one rule a reader can check by path ("from `state/cloud/` → `/cloud`").
2. **The 21 cloud names nobody outside the engine imports are not exported** by `/cloud`. They stay exported in their files, for the engine's own specs. Reason: the entry is the contract; a name enters it with its first consumer.
3. **Every consumer switches**: the functions, the game (its `admin-kit.ts` re-exports from `/cloud`, so the admin's imports stay as they are) and the remote's rules spec. A file that needs both takes two imports.
4. **Wiring**: the path `@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine/cloud` in `tsconfig.base.json`; the skip in `tools/federation/workspace-federation.js` beside the engine's other entries (the shell and every remote skip it alike); `engine-bundle.spec.ts` bundles `cloud.ts` too (Node only, no Angular, RxJS, Firebase). The `perf` bench bundles `index.ts` and uses no cloud name.
5. **Docs**: the root `CLAUDE.md` (Cloud Functions: "the documents … are described once, in the engine's `state/cloud/records/`", the federation skip list) and the engine's `CLAUDE.md`/`README.md` name the entry. `docs/architecture/README.md` is unchanged: no project and no edge is added.
6. **Release effect accepted**: the engine's, the game's and the functions' sources change, so the release redeploys `bacteria-wars-functions` and the game once, with code that behaves the same.

## Acceptance (step 3)

1. `src/index.ts` exports no name defined under `state/cloud/`; `src/cloud.ts` exports only such names (a spec over both entries' exported names checks it).
2. Outside the engine, no file imports a name of `state/cloud/` from the main entry (the TypeScript build fails where one does, since the name is gone).
3. Every name the main index exported before is exported by exactly one of the two entries afterwards, except the 21 unused cloud names (sorted lists compared, noted in the PR).
4. The engine's bundle check passes for `cloud.ts`; golden replays, GPU goldens and the `perf` checksums unchanged, no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump.
5. `npx nx affected -t lint,lint-templates,test,typecheck-specs,build` green, plus `bacteria-wars-functions:test`, `bacteria-wars-functions:build` and `bacteria-game-remote:build` (the federation build with the new skip).

## Open question (step 3)

- **The issue's "`src/index.ts` well under half its 791 lines"** is out of reach for `/cloud` alone: the cloud is 126 of 658 names, and the index ends at about 660 lines (about 84%). Options: (a) accept that for this step and restate the criterion as acceptance 1; (b) also drop, in this PR, the about 65 other names nobody outside the engine imports (about 600 lines); (c) add a later step of #3103 with a `/gpu` entry for the GPU mirror (84 names, the rendering lib's contract) plus that pruning, which brings the index to about 470 lines. Recommended: (a) now and (c) as step 3b, so this PR stays a pure move of the cloud contract.
EOF

2. **Consumers switch** (a scratch script moves each cloud name of an `@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine` import or `export … from` into a `/cloud` one, then `nx format:write`): `apps/bacteria-wars-functions/src/**`, `libs/features/lazy/bacteria-game/src/**` (`admin-kit.ts` included), `apps/bacteria-game-remote/src/firestore-rules-toggles.spec.ts`. 3. **Docs**: the root `CLAUDE.md`, the engine's `CLAUDE.md`/`README.md`. Commit `docs(feat-shared-bacteria-engine): name the /cloud entry`.
4. **Checks**: `npx nx format:write`; `npx nx affected -t lint,lint-templates,test,typecheck-specs,build`; `bacteria-wars-functions:test`, `:build`; `bacteria-game-remote:build`; `feat-shared-bacteria-engine:perf` checksums; the export lists compared.
EOF

reader can check by path ("from `state/cloud/` → `/cloud`").
2. **The 21 cloud names nobody outside the engine imports are not exported** by `/cloud`. They stay exported in their files, for the engine's own specs. Reason: the entry is the contract; a name enters it with its first consumer.
3. **Every consumer switches**: the functions, the game (its `admin-kit.ts` re-exports from `/cloud`, so the admin's imports stay as they are) and the remote's rules spec. A file that needs both takes two imports.
4. **Wiring**: the path `@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine/cloud` in `tsconfig.base.json`; the skip in `tools/federation/workspace-federation.js` beside the engine's other entries (the shell and every remote skip it alike); `engine-bundle.spec.ts` bundles `cloud.ts` too (Node only, no Angular, RxJS, Firebase). The `perf` bench bundles `index.ts` and uses no cloud name.
5. **Docs**: the root `CLAUDE.md` (Cloud Functions: "the documents … are described once, in the engine's `state/cloud/records/`", the federation skip list) and the engine's `CLAUDE.md` name the entry. `docs/architecture/README.md` is unchanged: no project and no edge is added.
6. **Release effect accepted**: the engine's, the game's and the functions' sources change, so the release redeploys `bacteria-wars-functions` and the game once, with code that behaves the same.

## Acceptance (step 3)

1. `src/index.ts` exports no name defined under `state/cloud/`; `src/cloud.ts` exports only such names (a spec over both entries' exported names checks it).
2. Outside the engine, no file imports a name of `state/cloud/` from the main entry (the TypeScript build fails where one does, since the name is gone).
3. Every name the main index exported before is exported by exactly one of the two entries afterwards, except the 21 unused cloud names (sorted lists compared, noted in the PR).
4. The engine's bundle check passes for `cloud.ts`; golden replays, GPU goldens and the `perf` checksums unchanged, no `BALANCE_VERSION` bump.
5. `npx nx affected -t lint,lint-templates,test,typecheck-specs,build` green, plus `bacteria-wars-functions:test`, `bacteria-wars-functions:build` and `bacteria-game-remote:build` (the federation build with the new skip).

## Open question (step 3)

- **The issue's "`src/index.ts` well under half its 791 lines"** is out of reach for `/cloud` alone: the cloud is 126 of 658 names, and the index ends at about 660 lines (about 84%). Options: (a) accept that for this step and restate the criterion as acceptance 1; (b) also drop, in this PR, the about 65 other names nobody outside the engine imports (about 600 lines); (c) add a later step of #3103 with a `/gpu` entry for the GPU mirror (84 names, the rendering lib's contract) plus that pruning, which brings the index to about 470 lines. Recommended: (a) now and (c) as step 3b, so this PR stays a pure move of the cloud contract.

# Bacteria engine

Rules for working on `libs/features/bacteria-engine`
(`feat-shared-bacteria-engine`), on top of the repo's `CLAUDE.md` and the
game lib's (`libs/features/lazy/bacteria-game/CLAUDE.md`), whose rules on
determinism, replays, balance and texts hold here too.

- The engine is the game without Angular: the match (`state/match/match-engine.ts`),
  both simulations, replays, levels, progress, achievements and the
  translation mechanics (`i18n/`). The game, its Cloud Functions
  (`apps/bacteria-wars-functions`) and the admin area play the same code.
- **Texts:** the engine holds only the English it renders into its state
  through `english()` (`ENGINE_EN` in `i18n/engine-texts.ts`: the areas
  `achievements`, `game`, `levels`, `training` under `i18n/en/`). Every
  other text, and all German, is the game's (`feat-lazy-bacteria-game`,
  `src/lib/i18n/texts/`), so a copy edit there reruns none of the engine's
  gates and deploys no function ([#3103](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/3103)). A key the engine builds goes into
  one of its four areas; `GameText<K>` is typed by the engine's keys
  (`EngineTextKey`) by default, the game widens it to its own.
- **Node only.** Nothing here imports Angular, NgRx, RxJS, Firebase, the
  DOM, `feat-bacteria-rendering` or `feat-bacteria-sound`. An oxlint override in
  `.oxlintrc.json` guards the imports, Jest runs every spec in Node
  (`testEnvironment: 'node'`), and `engine-bundle.spec.ts` bundles
  `src/index.ts` to prove it. Browser-only code goes elsewhere: WebGL and
  canvas into `feat-bacteria-rendering`, Web Audio into
  `feat-bacteria-sound`, the rest into the game lib.
- `src/index.ts` is the main entry (`@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine`):
  named exports, no `export *`. Nothing outside this lib imports a path
  inside it; a new export goes into the index. Spec fixtures (`aMatchRecord`,
  `recordedReplay`) are `@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine/testing`, for
  specs only. The balance lab (`state/balance/`, with the calibration's
  `SKILL` and `strengthOf`) is `@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine/balance`
  (`src/balance.ts`), for the scripts in `tools/bacteria-game/balance/`
  only; what they share with the game comes from the main entry.
- The targets `balance-check`, `balance` (ADR 0016) and `perf` (ADR 0014,
  `tools/perf/engine-bench.mjs`) live here, since they play the engine.
- The goldens (`state/replay/golden-replay.json`, `SELF_TEST_GOLDEN`) are guarded
  by their specs here; the GPU cross-check, which needs `gl/`, lives in
  `feat-bacteria-rendering` (`libs/features/bacteria-rendering/gpu-crosscheck/`)
  and imports the engine.
